books.section: Unit 5: Toward the Civil War and Reconstruction (1844–1877)

primary_sources: Fourteenth Amendment to the Constitution, Section 2 (ratified 1868)

stimulus.text:
“Representatives shall be apportioned among the several States according to their respective numbers, counting the whole number of persons in each State, excluding Indians not taxed. But when the right to vote at any election for the choice of electors for President and Vice-President of the United States, Representatives in Congress, the Executive and Judicial officers of a State, or the members of the Legislature thereof, is denied to any of the male inhabitants of such State, being twenty-one years of age, and citizens of the United States, or in any way abridged, except for participation in rebellion, or other crime, the basis of representation therein shall be reduced...”

—Fourteenth Amendment, Section 2, ratified 1868
stimulus.source_note: Fourteenth Amendment, Section 2, ratified 1868. Public domain. Wording verified against the Constitution Annotated (Congress.gov). Trailing ellipsis marks omitted text.

source: original; stimulus as noted in stimulus.source_note
stem: Elizabeth Cady Stanton and Susan B. Anthony opposed the Fifteenth Amendment because it

options.text: took the vote away from Black men.
options.misconception: Background: the amendment gave Black men the vote; it took it from no one.

options.text: gave women the vote only in the Southern states.
options.misconception: Background: the amendment gave women the vote nowhere, North or South.

options.text: was written by the Democratic Party.
options.misconception: Background: the amendment was the Republican Party’s work, and Stanton and Anthony opposed its limits, not its authors.

options.text: gave the vote to Black men but not to women.

rationales.A: Background: the amendment gave Black men the vote; it took it from no one.
rationales.B: Background: the amendment gave women the vote nowhere, North or South.
rationales.C: Background: the amendment was the Republican Party’s work, and Stanton and Anthony opposed its limits, not its authors.
rationales.D: The amendment bars denying the vote on account of race, and says nothing about sex. Stanton and Anthony refused to support an amendment that lifted Black men while leaving all women, Black and white, without the vote.
rationales.general:
1. The amendment’s promise covers race, color, and previous servitude.
2. Sex is missing from that list.
3. Background: Stanton and Anthony had fought for a universal right to vote, and this amendment drew a line that left women out.
4. So they opposed a victory they saw as half a victory.
Remember: a reform that helps one group can still divide its allies.
